question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

I have never seen a man / get off his horse quick as / did that stranger Englishman.
option_2: I have never seen a man
option_4: get off his horse quick as
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. get off his horse quick as.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "get off" is a verb, and a verb must be modified by an adverb, not by an adjective. "Quick" is an adjective; the adverb form is "quickly".

◦ Correct: I have never seen a man get off his horse quickly as did that stranger Englishman.

• The comparison here is about the manner of getting off the horse, so the adverb "quickly" is required.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "I have never seen a man" is correct — present perfect with "never" for experience.

• Option 1 "did that stranger Englishman." is a correct inverted structure after "as" (as did that stranger Englishman).

• Option 3 "No error" is wrong because a clear adjective/adverb error exists.

NOTE

• Adjective vs adverb: adjectives qualify nouns (a quick man), adverbs qualify verbs, adjectives and other adverbs (he ran quickly). Common SSC traps: quick/quickly, slow/slowly, loud/loudly, bad/badly.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required'.

(This bridge neither crossed the Thames, and neither gave) access to a now-lost island in the river.
option_1: This bridge either crossed the Thames, and or gave
option_2: This bridge neither crossed the Thames, nor gave
option_3: This bridge either crossed the Thames, nor gave
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. This bridge neither crossed the Thames, nor gave.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Neither" must always be paired with "nor" — they are correlative conjunctions. The printed sentence wrongly uses "neither ... and neither", which is incorrect.

◦ Correct: This bridge neither crossed the Thames, nor gave access to a now-lost island in the river.

• The two verbs joined ("crossed" and "gave") stay parallel in the simple past.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "either ... and or" mixes two pairs and is ungrammatical.

• Option 3 wrongly pairs "either" with "nor" — "either" goes with "or".

• Option 4 "No substitution required" is wrong because "and neither" cannot follow "neither".

NOTE

• Correlative pairs to memorise: either ... or, neither ... nor, not only ... but also, both ... and, whether ... or, no sooner ... than, hardly ... when. The parts joined must be grammatically parallel.

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

A thing that is kept as a reminder of a person, place, or event
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Souvenir.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "souvenir" is an object kept as a reminder of a person, place or event; a memento or keepsake. (स्मृति चिह्न / निशानी)

◦ Example: She bought a small brass elephant as a souvenir of her trip to Jaipur.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Sinecure" — a job or post that pays well but requires little or no work. (आरामतलब पद)

• Option 2 "Panacea" — a remedy said to cure all diseases and problems; a cure-all. (रामबाण)

• Option 4 "Regalia" — the emblems and rich robes of royalty (crown, sceptre, etc.) worn on ceremonial occasions. (राजचिह्न)

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes: memento/keepsake (a reminder), relic (an object surviving from the past), heirloom (a valuable object passed down in a family), memoir (a written account of one's own life).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Those unfamiliar with the saga are bound to be mystified by the more ______ plot twists.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. arcane.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Arcane" means mysterious, secret and understood by only a few people. Those unfamiliar with the saga would naturally be "mystified" by its more arcane (obscure) plot twists — the word matches "mystified" perfectly. (गूढ़ / रहस्यमय)

◦ Correct: Those unfamiliar with the saga are bound to be mystified by the more arcane plot twists.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "arbitrary" — based on random choice or personal whim rather than reason; does not connect with "mystified".

• Option 3 "aesthetic" — concerned with beauty or artistic taste; irrelevant here.

• Option 4 "anoint" — a verb meaning to smear with oil in a religious ceremony; grammatically impossible before a noun like "plot twists".

NOTE

• Synonyms of arcane: obscure, esoteric, cryptic, abstruse, recondite. Antonyms: obvious, plain, straightforward, well-known.

question: Select the wrongly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. eminant.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Eminant" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "eminent", meaning famous, distinguished and respected in a particular field. (प्रतिष्ठित / विख्यात)

◦ Spelling key: E + MI + NENT (all "e"s in the last two syllables, no "a").

◦ Example: An eminent scientist inaugurated the seminar.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "supersede" (to take the place of, to replace) is correctly spelt — note that it ends in "-sede", the only common English word to do so.

• "develop" (to grow or make progress) is correct — it has no "e" at the end.

• "quarantine" (a period of isolation to prevent the spread of disease) is correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Confusables: eminent (famous) / imminent (about to happen) / immanent (inherent). SSC frequently tests this trio.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Fixed in one's ways
option_1: Something that shows potential or looks promising in the beginning but fails to deliver anything in the end
option_3: Not willing or wanting to change from your normal way of doing something
option_4: An aggressive attack on someone by a group
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Not willing or wanting to change from your normal way of doing something.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "fixed (or set) in one's ways" means unwilling to change one's habits, opinions or normal way of doing things; rigid and resistant to new ideas. (अपने ढर्रे पर अड़ा रहना)

◦ Example: My grandfather is so fixed in his ways that he still refuses to use a mobile phone.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 describes the idiom "a damp squib" or "a flash in the pan" — something that begins promisingly but ends in failure.

• Option 2 "To establish one's rule" would suit an expression like "to hold sway".

• Option 4 "An aggressive attack on someone by a group" describes "to gang up on someone".

NOTE

• Similar idioms: "stuck in a rut" (in a boring unchanging routine), "old habits die hard", "creature of habit" (a person who likes a fixed routine).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym to substitute the bracketed word in the given sentence.

In the midst of the tumult of charges against him, a (welter) of conflicting poll numbers are being bandied about.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Turmoil.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "welter" means a large confused mass or jumble; a state of turmoil and disorder. Its closest synonym here is "turmoil" (great disturbance and confusion). (उथल-पुथल / अव्यवस्था)

◦ Example: A welter/turmoil of conflicting reports made the truth impossible to find.

• The context word "tumult" (uproar, commotion) in the same sentence confirms the sense of confusion.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Dynamic" — full of energy and change; it is not a noun of confusion.

• Option 3 "Static" — unchanging, still; the opposite of turmoil.

• Option 4 "Peace" — calm and quiet; also an antonym.

NOTE

• Synonyms of welter: turmoil, jumble, chaos, muddle, confusion. Note the phrase "bandied about" = (of rumours or figures) passed around casually.

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

His absence from my party is too much painful for me.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. party is too much.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Too much" is used before uncountable nouns (too much water, too much noise). Before an adjective such as "painful", we use only "too" (or "very").

◦ Correct: His absence from my party is too painful for me.

• So the segment "party is too much" wrongly inserts "much" before the adjective.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "His absence from my" is correct — "absence from" is the right collocation.

• Option 2 "painful for me." is correct — "painful for somebody".

• Option 4 "No error" is wrong because "too much + adjective" is ungrammatical.

NOTE

• Rules: too + adjective/adverb (too hot, too quickly); too much + uncountable noun (too much sugar); too many + countable plural (too many people); much too + adjective (much too hot) is also correct.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Our breathing rate can change almost instantaneously in response to stress or ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. arousal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Arousal" means a state of physiological excitement or heightened alertness in the body. Breathing rate changes instantly in response to stress or arousal — this is the standard physiological pairing. (उत्तेजना / सजगता की अवस्था)

◦ Correct: Our breathing rate can change almost instantaneously in response to stress or arousal.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "fund" (a sum of money) is completely unrelated to breathing.

• Option 3 "difference" is vague and does not name a bodily state.

• Option 4 "attention" is close in idea but does not itself trigger an instantaneous change in breathing the way stress/arousal does; "stress or arousal" is the natural collocation.

NOTE

• Word family: arouse (verb — to stir up), arousal (noun), aroused (adjective). Do not confuse with "arise" (to happen/come into being).

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate choice.

The issue of fairness, which remained, was for consideration at the hearing to ______ the scheme.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. sanction.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Sanction" as a verb means to give official permission or approval for something. A hearing is held "to sanction the scheme", i.e., to formally approve it. (मंजूरी देना / अनुमोदन करना)

◦ Correct: ... was for consideration at the hearing to sanction the scheme.

• The blank follows "to", so a verb is required — only "sanction" works as a verb here.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "acclamation" — loud and enthusiastic approval (a noun, not a verb).

• Option 3 "altercation" — a noisy argument or quarrel (a noun).

• Option 4 "stratification" — arrangement into layers or classes (a noun).

NOTE

• "Sanction" is a contronym: as a noun it can mean approval (government sanction) or a penalty (economic sanctions against a country). Context decides the meaning.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

The final cost depends on whether you chooses the small or the large size.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. choose the small.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject is "you", which is a plural-type subject, so the verb must be the base form "choose", not the third-person singular "chooses".

◦ Correct: The final cost depends on whether you choose the small or the large size.

• The adjective must remain "small" so that it stays parallel with "the large size" that follows.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "choose the smaller" fixes the verb but breaks the parallelism — "smaller ... or the large" is inconsistent.

• Option 2 "chose the small" wrongly shifts to the past tense while the main verb "depends" is in the present.

• Option 3 "No improvement" is wrong because "you chooses" is a clear subject-verb agreement error.

NOTE

• Subject-verb agreement: I/we/you/they + base verb (choose); he/she/it + verb + s (chooses). "You" always takes the plural verb form, even when it refers to one person.

question:
Select the appropriate synonym for the underlined word.

She goes to her room and locks herself in.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Shuts.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Locks (oneself in)" means to fasten a door so that no one can enter, thereby shutting oneself inside. Its closest synonym among the options is "shuts" (shuts herself in). (बंद कर लेना)

◦ Example: Whenever she is upset, she locks/shuts herself in her room.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "taunts" — mocks or jeers at someone. (ताना मारना)

• Option 2 "hurts" — causes pain or injury. (चोट पहुँचाना)

• Option 3 "sinks" — goes down below the surface. (डूबना)

NOTE

• Synonyms of lock: shut, fasten, bolt, latch, secure. Antonyms: unlock, open, unfasten. Phrasal uses: "lock up" (secure a building), "lock out" (keep someone outside), "lock in" (confine inside).

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

Cold fish
option_2: To make a lot of money
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. A person lacking in sympathy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "a cold fish" refers to a person who is unemotional, unfriendly and lacking in warmth or sympathy. (भावनाहीन / रूखा व्यक्ति)

◦ Example: The new manager is such a cold fish that no one dares to share their problems with him.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "To make a lot of money" corresponds to idioms like "to make a killing" or "to rake it in".

• Option 3 "A dead body" is a literal misreading, not the idiomatic sense.

• Option 4 "To retract one's statements" matches "to eat one's words" or "to backtrack".

NOTE

• Other "fish" idioms: "a big fish in a small pond" (an important person in a small group), "fish out of water" (uncomfortable in unfamiliar surroundings), "other fish to fry" (more important things to do).

question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

Neither she ______ I have expected Reema's arrival.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. nor.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Neither" is always followed by its correlative partner "nor". Therefore the blank must be filled with "nor".

◦ Correct: Neither she nor I have expected Reema's arrival.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "or" goes with "either", not "neither".

• Option 2 "and" and Option 4 "along" cannot complete the "neither ..." structure.

NOTE

• With "neither ... nor" and "either ... or", the verb agrees with the nearer subject (proximity rule): "Neither she nor I have...", "Neither the boys nor the teacher is present.

question:
Choose the word that can substitute the given group of words.

Famous or well-known for a negative reason
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Notorious.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Notorious" means famous or well-known, but for a bad quality or deed. It is the exact one-word substitute for the given group of words. (कुख्यात / बदनाम)

◦ Example: The area is notorious for its traffic jams.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Unpopular" merely means disliked; it does not imply fame.

• Option 2 "Reputable" means having a good reputation — the opposite sense.

• Option 3 "Formidable" means inspiring fear or respect through being impressively powerful.

NOTE

• Contrast: famous/renowned/illustrious (well-known for good reasons) vs notorious/infamous (well-known for bad reasons). The noun form is "notoriety".

question:
Select the appropriate antonym for the underlined word.

Sunny turned to find his daughter's sweet, bright eyes close to his.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. dusky.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Bright" here means shining, full of light and sparkle. Its antonym is "dusky", meaning dim, dark and shadowy. (चमकीला का विलोम — धुँधला / श्यामल)

◦ Example: The bright morning sky slowly turned dusky at sunset.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "gleaming" (shining brightly) is a synonym of bright, not an antonym.

• Option 3 "merry" (cheerful) is close to the "cheerful" sense of bright, again a synonym.

• Option 4 "anxious" (worried) is unrelated to brightness.

NOTE

• Synonyms of bright: shining, radiant, gleaming, luminous, brilliant. Antonyms: dull, dim, dusky, murky, gloomy, sombre.

question: Choose the incorrectly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Potantial.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Potantial" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "potential", meaning having the capacity to develop into something in the future; possible latent ability. (संभावित / क्षमता)

◦ Spelling key: PO + TEN + TIAL (an "e" in the middle, not an "a").

◦ Example: She has enormous potential as an athlete.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Grease" (thick oily lubricant) is correctly spelt.

• "Mimic" (to imitate someone) is correctly spelt — note it doubles the "k" only in "mimicking / mimicked".

• "Surge" (a sudden powerful forward movement or increase) is correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Words with the "-tial" ending: potential, essential, influential, confidential, substantial, partial. Related forms: potential (adjective/noun), potentially (adverb), potentiality (noun).

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Why are you making excuses too avoid this work?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. making excuses too.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence needs the infinitive marker "to" before the verb "avoid" (making excuses to avoid this work). The word printed is "too" (meaning "also / excessively"), which is wrong here.

◦ Correct: Why are you making excuses to avoid this work?

• "to + base verb" expresses purpose — the excuses are made in order to avoid the work.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Why are you" is a correct present-continuous interrogative structure.

• Option 1 "avoid this work?" is correct as the base verb after "to".

• Option 3 "No error" is wrong because of the to/too confusion.

NOTE

• Homophone trio: to (preposition / infinitive marker), too (also, excessively), two (the number 2). SSC tests this pair very frequently in spotting-error questions.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

The camel uses fat as a source of energy during its longer journey in the desert.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. its long journey.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The comparative degree "longer" cannot be used here because no comparison is being made and there is no "than". The simple positive degree "long" is required.

◦ Correct: The camel uses fat as a source of energy during its long journey in the desert.

• "Its" (possessive adjective) is correct before "long journey".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "No improvement" is wrong because the unnecessary comparative is an error.

• Option 2 "it's longer journey" wrongly uses "it's", which is the contraction of "it is / it has", not a possessive.

• Option 3 "its longest journeyed" mixes a superlative with a past-participle form and is meaningless.

NOTE

• Its = belonging to it (The dog wagged its tail). It's = it is / it has (It's raining). Use the comparative (longer) only with "than" and the superlative (longest) only with "the".

question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

Mound
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Valley.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "mound" is a raised mass of earth; a small hill or heap. Its antonym is "valley", which is a low area of land between hills or mountains. (टीला का विलोम — घाटी)

◦ Example: The children climbed the grassy mound, while the river flowed through the valley below.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Victory" (a win) is unrelated to landforms.

• Option 3 "Bell" (a hollow metal instrument that rings) is unrelated.

• Option 4 "Prominence" (something that juts out; the state of being important) is closer to a synonym of a raised feature, not an antonym.

NOTE

• Synonyms of mound: hillock, heap, knoll, hummock, pile. Antonyms: valley, hollow, depression, basin, ditch.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Archaeologists believe that counting large quantities (1) ______ about 10,000 years ago. Early farmers had to (2) ______ for communally stored crops. Early counting systems involved small tokens which represented farmers' stores. In the area which is now southern Iraq, little figures shaped like discs, balls, and pyramids (3) ______ used in about 7500 B.C. to represent various holdings. Later, marks which represented the figures were (4) ______ on clay tablets by use of a blunt reed to cut into the wet clay. Still, the symbols were (5) ______ connected with specific merchandise.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. began.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage traces the origin of counting: archaeologists believe that counting large quantities "began about 10,000 years ago". "Began" (past tense of "begin") means started. (आरंभ हुआ)

◦ Correct: Archaeologists believe that counting large quantities began about 10,000 years ago.

• The whole passage then goes on to describe how counting developed afterwards, which confirms that a starting point is being stated.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "blessed" (made holy / brought good fortune) makes no sense with "counting".

• Option 2 "allured" (tempted or attracted) does not fit an activity beginning.

• Option 3 "ended" is the opposite of the intended sense — counting clearly did not stop 10,000 years ago.

NOTE

• Verb forms: begin – began – begun. Use "began" for the simple past and "begun" only after have/has/had.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Archaeologists believe that counting large quantities (1) ______ about 10,000 years ago. Early farmers had to (2) ______ for communally stored crops. Early counting systems involved small tokens which represented farmers' stores. In the area which is now southern Iraq, little figures shaped like discs, balls, and pyramids (3) ______ used in about 7500 B.C. to represent various holdings. Later, marks which represented the figures were (4) ______ on clay tablets by use of a blunt reed to cut into the wet clay. Still, the symbols were (5) ______ connected with specific merchandise.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. account.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank is followed by the preposition "for", and the fixed phrasal verb is "account for", meaning to give a reckoning of; to explain or keep a record of. Early farmers had to account for communally stored crops. (हिसाब रखना / लेखा देना)

◦ Correct: Early farmers had to account for communally stored crops.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "discount" means to deduct an amount or to disregard; "discount for" is not the required expression.

• Option 2 "count" would need "count" the crops, not "count for" them — "count for" means "to be of value", which does not fit.

• Option 4 "undercount" means to count fewer than the actual number — the opposite of careful record-keeping.

NOTE

• Common uses of "account": account for (explain / form a part of), on account of (because of), take into account (consider), call to account (demand an explanation).

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Archaeologists believe that counting large quantities (1) ______ about 10,000 years ago. Early farmers had to (2) ______ for communally stored crops. Early counting systems involved small tokens which represented farmers' stores. In the area which is now southern Iraq, little figures shaped like discs, balls, and pyramids (3) ______ used in about 7500 B.C. to represent various holdings. Later, marks which represented the figures were (4) ______ on clay tablets by use of a blunt reed to cut into the wet clay. Still, the symbols were (5) ______ connected with specific merchandise.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. were.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject is "little figures shaped like discs, balls, and pyramids", which is plural, and the time reference is "in about 7500 B.C.", which is past. Hence the past plural auxiliary "were" is required to form the passive "were used".

◦ Correct: ... little figures shaped like discs, balls, and pyramids were used in about 7500 B.C. ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "are" is present tense — wrong, since the sentence describes 7500 B.C.

• Option 2 "will be" is future tense — impossible for an ancient event.

• Option 3 "was" is singular and does not agree with the plural subject "figures".

NOTE

• Passive voice: was/were + past participle for the past (were used), is/are + past participle for the present (are used). Always match the auxiliary with the number of the subject.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Archaeologists believe that counting large quantities (1) ______ about 10,000 years ago. Early farmers had to (2) ______ for communally stored crops. Early counting systems involved small tokens which represented farmers' stores. In the area which is now southern Iraq, little figures shaped like discs, balls, and pyramids (3) ______ used in about 7500 B.C. to represent various holdings. Later, marks which represented the figures were (4) ______ on clay tablets by use of a blunt reed to cut into the wet clay. Still, the symbols were (5) ______ connected with specific merchandise.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. inscribed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Inscribed" means written, carved or engraved on a surface. The passage says the marks were cut into wet clay tablets with a blunt reed — that is exactly inscribing. (उत्कीर्ण करना / अंकित करना)

◦ Correct: ... marks which represented the figures were inscribed on clay tablets ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "transcribed" means to copy out written material or convert speech into writing — the marks were not being copied from anywhere.

• Option 3 "prescribed" means to lay down a rule or to order a medicine.

• Option 4 "subscribed" means to pay to receive a publication or to give one's support/signature.

NOTE

• The root "scribe" (to write) gives: inscribe (write on), describe (write about), prescribe (write beforehand/order), transcribe (write across/copy), subscribe (write under/sign up), ascribe (attribute).

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Archaeologists believe that counting large quantities (1) ______ about 10,000 years ago. Early farmers had to (2) ______ for communally stored crops. Early counting systems involved small tokens which represented farmers' stores. In the area which is now southern Iraq, little figures shaped like discs, balls, and pyramids (3) ______ used in about 7500 B.C. to represent various holdings. Later, marks which represented the figures were (4) ______ on clay tablets by use of a blunt reed to cut into the wet clay. Still, the symbols were (5) ______ connected with specific merchandise.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. always.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs an adverb of frequency between the verb "were" and the participle "connected". "Always" (at all times, invariably) fits perfectly and matches the contrast word "Still" at the start of the sentence — even at that stage, the symbols were always tied to specific goods.

◦ Correct: Still, the symbols were always connected with specific merchandise.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "like" is a preposition/conjunction and cannot stand between "were" and "connected".

• Option 3 "some" is a determiner used before nouns, not before a past participle.

• Option 4 "just" would change the meaning to "only recently / merely" and does not suit the contrast introduced by "Still".

NOTE

• Adverbs of frequency (always, often, usually, never, sometimes) are placed after the auxiliary verb "be" (She is always late) and before the main verb (She always comes late).

question: Krishna River flows through ______ state of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karnataka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Krishna River rises at Mahabaleshwar in Maharashtra (Western Ghats) and flows eastwards through Karnataka and Telangana before entering Andhra Pradesh, where it drains into the Bay of Bengal. (कृष्णा नदी — कर्नाटक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Krishna is the second longest river of peninsular India (about 1,400 km) after the Godavari.

• Its major tributaries are the Bhima, Tungabhadra, Koyna, Ghataprabha, Malaprabha and Musi.

• Important dams on the Krishna basin: Almatti and Narayanpur (Karnataka), Srisailam and Nagarjuna Sagar (Andhra Pradesh/Telangana).

NOTE

• The Krishna does not flow through Tamil Nadu, Odisha or Kerala. Peninsular east-flowing rivers: Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri — all draining into the Bay of Bengal.

question: Who among the following sang the famous Bollywood song "Ae Dil Hai Mushkil"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arijit Singh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The famous Bollywood title track "Ae Dil Hai Mushkil" (from the 2016 film of the same name) was sung by Arijit Singh. The music was composed by Pritam and the lyrics were written by Amitabh Bhattacharya. (अरिजीत सिंह)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Arijit Singh rose to fame with "Tum Hi Ho" (Aashiqui 2) and has won the National Film Award for Best Male Playback Singer and several Filmfare Awards.

• The film "Ae Dil Hai Mushkil" was directed by Karan Johar.

NOTE

• Neeti Mohan and Shreya Ghoshal are leading female playback singers; Sukhbir is known chiefly for Punjabi pop songs such as "Ishq Tera Tadpave".

question: In which of the following Articles is "Protection against arrest and detention" mentioned?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 22.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 22 of the Indian Constitution provides "Protection against arrest and detention in certain cases". It guarantees an arrested person the right to be informed of the grounds of arrest, the right to consult a lawyer of his choice, and the right to be produced before a magistrate within 24 hours of arrest (excluding travel time). (अनुच्छेद 22 — गिरफ्तारी और निरोध से संरक्षण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Article 20 — Protection in respect of conviction for offences (no ex-post-facto law, no double jeopardy, no self-incrimination).

• Article 21 — Protection of life and personal liberty; Article 21A — Right to Education.

• Article 24 — Prohibition of employment of children below 14 years in factories, mines and hazardous work.

• Article 18 — Abolition of titles.

NOTE

• Articles 19–22 together form the Right to Freedom. Article 22 also lays down safeguards regarding preventive detention (normally not beyond 3 months without an Advisory Board's opinion).

question: The Airavatesvara Temple in Tamil Nadu was built by ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajaraja Chola II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Airavatesvara Temple at Darasuram (Kumbakonam), Thanjavur district, Tamil Nadu, was built by the Chola king Rajaraja Chola II in the 12th century CE. It is dedicated to Lord Shiva. (ऐरावतेश्वर मंदिर — राजराज चोल द्वितीय)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• It is one of the "Great Living Chola Temples", a UNESCO World Heritage Site, along with the Brihadeeswarar Temple at Thanjavur (built by Rajaraja Chola I) and the Brihadeeswarar Temple at Gangaikonda Cholapuram (built by Rajendra Chola I).

• The temple takes its name from Airavata, the white elephant of Indra, who is said to have worshipped Shiva here.

NOTE

• The Chola temples are the finest examples of Dravidian architecture, with a towering vimana, a pillared mandapa and elaborate stone sculptures.

question: Which of the following is the first month in the Islamic lunar calendar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Muharram.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Muharram" is the first month of the Islamic (Hijri) lunar calendar. It is one of the four sacred months in Islam, and its 10th day (Ashura) is observed in remembrance of the martyrdom of Imam Hussain at the Battle of Karbala. (मुहर्रम — इस्लामी कैलेंडर का पहला महीना)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The twelve months of the Hijri calendar in order: Muharram, Safar, Rabi' al-Awwal, Rabi' al-Thani, Jumada al-Awwal, Jumada al-Thani, Rajab, Sha'ban, Ramadan, Shawwal, Dhu al-Qi'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah.

• Ramzan (Ramadan) is the 9th month, the month of fasting; Shawwal is the 10th month, and Eid-ul-Fitr is celebrated on its first day.

NOTE

• The Islamic calendar is purely lunar with 354/355 days, so its months shift about 10–11 days earlier each year relative to the Gregorian calendar. It began with the Hijra (migration of Prophet Muhammad from Mecca to Medina) in 622 CE.

question: The materials, through which things cannot be seen, are called ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is opaque materials.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Opaque materials" are those through which light cannot pass at all, so objects on the other side cannot be seen. Examples: wood, stone, metal, cardboard, a brick wall. (अपारदर्शी पदार्थ)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Transparent materials allow light to pass through completely, so objects are seen clearly — e.g., clear glass, water, air.

• Translucent materials allow light to pass partially, so objects are seen hazily/blurred — e.g., butter paper, frosted glass, oiled paper.

• "Pale" simply means light in colour and is not an optical classification.

NOTE

• Opaque objects form sharp shadows because they block light completely. The formation of shadows and eclipses depends on light travelling in straight lines (rectilinear propagation).

question: There were several cities in the Maurya empire. Which of the following cities was located on the southernmost side?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Brahmagiri.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Among the given Mauryan centres, "Brahmagiri" (in present-day Chitradurga district, Karnataka) lay the furthest south. It is famous for a set of Ashokan minor rock edicts and marks the southern reach of the Mauryan empire. (ब्रह्मगिरि — सबसे दक्षिणी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Girnar (Junagadh, Gujarat) — site of Ashoka's Major Rock Edicts and later the Rudradaman inscription on the Sudarshana Lake.

• Topra (Haryana) — the original site of the pillar later moved to Delhi by Firoz Shah Tughlaq (Delhi-Topra pillar).

• Rupnath (Madhya Pradesh) — site of an Ashokan minor rock edict.

NOTE

• Mauryan provincial capitals: Pataliputra (imperial capital), Taxila (north-west), Ujjain (west), Tosali (east/Kalinga) and Suvarnagiri (south). The empire's southern limit stopped short of the Tamil kingdoms (Cholas, Cheras, Pandyas).

question: Kitab ul-Hind, an Arabic text was written by ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Al- Biruni.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Kitab-ul-Hind" (also called Tahqiq-i-Hind) is an Arabic work written by Al-Biruni, the Central Asian scholar who came to India in the 11th century along with Mahmud of Ghazni. It describes Indian religion, philosophy, sciences, customs, astronomy and the caste system. (किताब-उल-हिंद — अलबरूनी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Ibn Battuta, a Moroccan traveller who visited India during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq, wrote "Rihla" (in Arabic).

• Ziauddin Barani wrote "Tarikh-i-Firuz Shahi" and "Fatwa-i-Jahandari" (in Persian).

• Sultan Mahmud of Ghazni was the invader who raided India seventeen times, most famously sacking the Somnath temple (1025 CE).

NOTE

• Al-Biruni is often called the "Father of Indology". He learnt Sanskrit and studied the Vedas, the Puranas, the Bhagavad Gita and works of Indian mathematics and astronomy.

question: The Weapons of Mass Destruction and their Delivery Systems (Prohibition of Unlawful Activities) Amendment Bill-2022 is related to which ______ of the Government of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of External Affairs.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Weapons of Mass Destruction and their Delivery Systems (Prohibition of Unlawful Activities) Amendment Bill, 2022" was introduced in Parliament by the Ministry of External Affairs. It amends the parent Act of 2005 to additionally prohibit the financing of any activity related to weapons of mass destruction and their delivery systems. (विदेश मंत्रालय)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Weapons of Mass Destruction (WMD) include biological, chemical and nuclear weapons.

• The amendment empowers the Central Government to freeze, seize or attach funds and other financial assets of persons suspected of such financing.

• It brings India's law in line with the requirements of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) and UN Security Council Resolution 1540.

NOTE

• India follows a "No First Use" (NFU) nuclear doctrine and maintains a policy of credible minimum deterrence. India is a member of the MTCR, Wassenaar Arrangement and Australia Group, though not of the NSG.

question: Gulabo Sapera is associated with which of the following dance forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kalbelia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Gulabo Sapera is the renowned exponent who popularised the "Kalbelia" folk dance of Rajasthan on the world stage. She was awarded the Padma Shri in 2016. (कालबेलिया नृत्य — गुलाबो सपेरा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Kalbelia is performed by the women of the Kalbelia (snake-charmer) community of Rajasthan; the swirling black skirts and serpentine movements imitate a snake's motion.

• It was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010.

• Instruments used include the been (pungi), khanjari, dholak and morchang.

NOTE

• Other Rajasthani folk dances: Ghoomar, Bhavai, Chari, Terah Taali and Kachhi Ghodi. Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Odissi (Odisha) and Kathakali (Kerala) are classical, not folk, forms.

question: Which of the following acids makes the pH of vinegar acidic?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Acetic acid.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vinegar is a dilute (about 5–8%) aqueous solution of "acetic acid (CH₃COOH)", which is what makes its pH acidic (roughly 2.4–3.4). Acetic acid is a weak carboxylic acid with the common name ethanoic acid. (सिरका — ऐसीटिक अम्ल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Tartaric acid — found in tamarind and grapes; used in baking powder.

• Citric acid — found in lemon, orange and other citrus fruits.

• Linoleic acid — an essential fatty acid found in vegetable oils, not a food acidulant.

NOTE

• Natural acids: lactic acid (curd/milk), oxalic acid (tomato, spinach), malic acid (apple), formic acid (ant sting), butyric acid (rancid butter), ascorbic acid (Vitamin C, amla). Glacial acetic acid is pure (nearly 100%) acetic acid, which freezes below 16.6°C.

question: How many bronze medals did India win in the Tokyo Olympics 2020 (held in the year 2021)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Four.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• At the Tokyo Olympics 2020 (held in July–August 2021 due to the COVID-19 pandemic), India won a total of 7 medals — 1 gold, 2 silver and 4 bronze, its best-ever Olympic haul. (टोक्यो ओलंपिक 2020 — 4 कांस्य पदक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Gold (1): Neeraj Chopra — Javelin throw (India's first-ever Olympic gold in athletics).

• Silver (2): Mirabai Chanu (weightlifting, 49 kg) and Ravi Kumar Dahiya (wrestling, 57 kg).

• Bronze (4): P. V. Sindhu (badminton), Lovlina Borgohain (boxing, 69 kg), Bajrang Punia (wrestling, 65 kg) and the Indian Men's Hockey Team (its first Olympic medal in 41 years).

NOTE

• P. V. Sindhu became the first Indian woman to win two individual Olympic medals (silver at Rio 2016, bronze at Tokyo 2020). India finished 48th on the Tokyo medal tally.

question: Savings deposits with Post Office savings banks are included in which measure of money supply?
solution_text:
The correct answer is M2.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the RBI's classification of money supply, "M2" = M1 + savings deposits with Post Office savings banks. Hence Post Office savings deposits first appear in M2. (एम2 — डाकघर बचत जमा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• M1 (narrow money) = Currency with the public + Demand deposits with the banking system + "Other" deposits with the RBI.

• M2 = M1 + Savings deposits with Post Office savings banks.

• M3 (broad money) = M1 + Time deposits with the banking system — this is the most widely used aggregate monetary resource.

• M4 = M3 + All deposits with Post Office savings banks (excluding National Savings Certificates).

NOTE

• Liquidity order: M1 > M2 > M3 > M4 (M1 is the most liquid, M4 the least). M1 and M2 are called narrow money, while M3 and M4 are called broad money.

question: According to the 2011 census, what is the approximate female literacy rate?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 65%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census of India 2011, the female literacy rate was about 65.46% (approximately 65%), while the male literacy rate was about 82.14% and the overall literacy rate was 74.04%. (2011 जनगणना — महिला साक्षरता लगभग 65%)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kerala had the highest literacy rate (94%) and Bihar the lowest (61.8%) in Census 2011.

• Sex ratio (2011) — 943 females per 1000 males; Kerala highest (1084), Haryana lowest (879).

• A person aged 7 years and above who can both read and write with understanding in any language is counted as literate.

NOTE

• Census 2011 was the 15th national census and the 7th since Independence. The first synchronous census in India was held in 1881 under Lord Ripon.

question: Which of the following statement is NOT correct regarding fertilizers?
option_2: They are very rich in plant nutrients
option_3: They provide humus to the soil
solution_text:
The correct answer is They provide humus to the soil.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Fertilizers do NOT provide humus to the soil — this statement is incorrect. Humus is supplied by manure (organic matter such as decomposed plant and animal waste), not by chemical fertilizers. (उर्वरक मिट्टी को ह्यूमस नहीं देते)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The other statements are correct: fertilizers are prepared in factories, are man-made inorganic salts, and are rich in specific plant nutrients (N, P, K).

• Examples of fertilizers: urea, ammonium sulphate, superphosphate, NPK, potash.

NOTE

• Manure vs Fertilizer — Manure: natural/organic, adds humus, improves soil texture and water-holding capacity, nutrient-poor per unit. Fertilizer: chemical/inorganic, nutrient-rich, gives quick results, but excessive use causes soil degradation and water eutrophication.

question: What is the term of State legislative assembly in India as per Indian constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 5 years.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The normal term of a State Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) is five years from the date of its first meeting, unless dissolved earlier by the Governor. (विधान सभा का कार्यकाल — 5 वर्ष)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• During a National Emergency (Article 352), the term may be extended by Parliament by one year at a time, but not beyond six months after the Emergency ceases.

• The Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) is a permanent house that is never dissolved; one-third of its members retire every two years, and each member has a term of six years.

• The Lok Sabha also has a normal term of 5 years; the Rajya Sabha is permanent.

NOTE

• Minimum age: 25 years for the Legislative Assembly and 30 years for the Legislative Council. The maximum strength of an Assembly is 500 and the minimum is 60 (with special exceptions such as Sikkim, Goa and Mizoram).

question: When was the Gandhi-Irwin pact signed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1931.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Gandhi-Irwin Pact" was signed on 5 March 1931 in Delhi between Mahatma Gandhi and Lord Irwin, the then Viceroy of India. Under it, Gandhi agreed to suspend the Civil Disobedience Movement and attend the Second Round Table Conference in London. (गांधी-इरविन समझौता — 1931)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• In return, the Government agreed to release political prisoners (not those guilty of violence), withdraw ordinances, return confiscated property and allow the peaceful picketing of liquor and foreign-cloth shops and the making of salt for personal use in coastal areas.

• It is also known as the Delhi Pact. Gandhi attended the Second Round Table Conference (1931) as the sole representative of the Congress.

NOTE

• Timeline: Simon Commission — 1928; Lahore Session/Purna Swaraj — 1929; Dandi March/Civil Disobedience — 1930; Gandhi-Irwin Pact — 1931; Poona Pact — 1932; Government of India Act — 1935.

question: The weather pattern of a place, made on the basis of the aggregate weather data collected over a long period, such as 25 years, is called the ______ of that place.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Climate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Climate" is the sum total (average) of the weather conditions of a place over a long period, generally taken as 25 to 30 years or more. It describes the general pattern, whereas weather describes the atmospheric condition at a particular time and place. (जलवायु)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Elements of weather and climate: temperature, atmospheric pressure, wind, humidity and precipitation.

• Factors controlling climate: latitude, altitude, distance from the sea, ocean currents, relief and prevailing winds.

• India has a tropical monsoon climate, dominated by the seasonal reversal of winds.

NOTE

• "Ecology" is the study of the relationship between organisms and their surroundings; "landforms" are the physical features of the Earth's surface; "environment" is the total surroundings (biotic + abiotic) of an organism.

question: Which of the following books was NOT written by Aravind Adiga?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Cost of Living.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The Cost of Living" was NOT written by Aravind Adiga — it is a collection of essays by Arundhati Roy (1999), dealing with big dams and India's development policy. (द कॉस्ट ऑफ लिविंग — अरुंधति रॉय)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Books written by Aravind Adiga: "The White Tiger" (winner of the Man Booker Prize, 2008), "Between the Assassinations", "Last Man in Tower", "Selection Day" and "Amnesty".

• The White Tiger was adapted into a Netflix film in 2021.

NOTE

• Arundhati Roy won the Booker Prize in 1997 for "The God of Small Things"; her other works include "The Ministry of Utmost Happiness" and "Walking with the Comrades". Other Indian-origin Booker winners: V. S. Naipaul (1971), Salman Rushdie (1981), Kiran Desai (2006).

question: The British Parliament passed the Regulating Act in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1773.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Regulating Act was passed by the British Parliament in 1773. It was the first step by the British Government to control and regulate the affairs of the East India Company in India. (रेगुलेटिंग एक्ट — 1773)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Key provisions of the Regulating Act, 1773:

◦ It designated the Governor of Bengal as the "Governor-General of Bengal" — Warren Hastings became the first — and created an Executive Council of four members.

◦ It made the Governors of Bombay and Madras subordinate to the Governor-General of Bengal.

◦ It provided for the establishment of a Supreme Court at Calcutta (1774) with one Chief Justice and three other judges.

◦ It prohibited Company servants from engaging in private trade and accepting bribes or gifts from Indians.

NOTE

• Later constitutional landmarks: Pitt's India Act (1784), Charter Act of 1813/1833/1853, Government of India Act 1858 (Crown rule), Indian Councils Acts 1861/1892/1909, Government of India Acts 1919 and 1935.

question: On 8 September 2022, NITI Aayog, in collaboration with ______, launched the country's first national electric freight platform - Electric Freight Accelerator for Sustainable Transport - India (e-FAST India).
solution_text:
The correct answer is World Resources Institute.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• On 8 September 2022, NITI Aayog, in collaboration with the "World Resources Institute (WRI) India", launched India's first national electric freight platform — e-FAST India (Electric Freight Accelerator for Sustainable Transport - India). (विश्व संसाधन संस्थान)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• e-FAST India aims to accelerate the electrification of freight/trucking in India by building awareness, supporting pilot projects and enabling policy dialogue among stakeholders.

• The platform was supported by the Council on Energy, Environment and Water (CEEW) and the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, among others.

• Freight transport contributes a large share of transport-sector CO₂ emissions in India, so electrifying trucks is central to the net-zero-by-2070 goal.

NOTE

• NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) replaced the Planning Commission on 1 January 2015. Its Chairperson is the Prime Minister, and it has a Vice-Chairperson and a CEO.

question: By the New Delhi International Arbitration Centre (Amendment) Bill, 2022, the period given to the Central Government for removing any difficulty arising in giving effect to the New Delhi International Arbitration Centre Act, 2019 has been extended to ______ years from the date of commencement of the Act.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 5.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "New Delhi International Arbitration Centre (Amendment) Bill, 2022" extended the time available to the Central Government to issue orders removing difficulties in giving effect to the parent Act from two years to five years from the date of commencement of the Act. (5 वर्ष)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The New Delhi International Arbitration Centre Act, 2019 set up the NDIAC as an institution of national importance to promote institutional arbitration in India.

• The 2022 amendment also renamed the centre as the "India International Arbitration Centre".

• "Removal of difficulties" clauses are a standard feature of Indian statutes, allowing the Government to issue clarifying orders within a limited window.

NOTE

• Arbitration in India is chiefly governed by the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 (amended in 2015, 2019 and 2021), which is based on the UNCITRAL Model Law.

question: Kajari is a folk song and dance style of India. It originated in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Kajari (Kajri)" is a semi-classical folk song and dance form that originated in Uttar Pradesh, particularly in the Mirzapur, Varanasi and Bhojpuri-speaking region. It is sung during the monsoon month of Sawan (Bhadon) and expresses the longing of a wife for her husband who is away. (कजरी — उत्तर प्रदेश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kajari is closely associated with the Kajari Teej festival and is traditionally sung by women in groups during the rainy season.

• Other folk traditions of Uttar Pradesh: Birha, Chaiti, Sohar, Rasiya, Charkula, Nautanki, Raslila and Khyal.

NOTE

• Regional folk forms: Bhangra/Giddha (Punjab), Baul/Chhau (West Bengal), Ottamthullal/Theyyam (Kerala), Lavani (Maharashtra), Bihu (Assam), Garba (Gujarat).

question: In cricket, hitting the ball in the air in such a way that it goes beyond the boundary is equal to ______ runs.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 6.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In cricket, if the batter strikes the ball so that it clears the boundary without touching the ground inside the field, the batting side is awarded six (6) runs. (छक्का — 6 रन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• If the ball touches the ground before crossing (or rolls over) the boundary, four (4) runs are awarded.

• Cricket's laws are framed by the Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC), and the sport is governed internationally by the International Cricket Council (ICC), headquartered in Dubai, UAE.

• The BCCI (Board of Control for Cricket in India) was established in 1928.

NOTE

• Cricket terms: over (6 legal balls), maiden over (no runs conceded), hat-trick (three wickets in three consecutive balls), duck (dismissed for zero), century (100 runs), LBW (leg before wicket). Yuvraj Singh famously hit six sixes in an over against England in the 2007 T20 World Cup.

question: According to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution, India is a ______ country.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Republic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Preamble of the Indian Constitution declares India to be a "SOVEREIGN SOCIALIST SECULAR DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC". A "Republic" means the head of the State (the President) is elected and not a hereditary monarch, and every public office is open to every citizen without discrimination. (गणराज्य)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The words "SOCIALIST", "SECULAR" and "INTEGRITY" were added to the Preamble by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.

• The Preamble secures to all citizens Justice (social, economic and political), Liberty (of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship), Equality (of status and opportunity) and promotes Fraternity (assuring the dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the Nation).

• The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950.

NOTE

• The Preamble is based on the Objectives Resolution moved by Jawaharlal Nehru in 1946. In the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973), the Supreme Court held that the Preamble is a part of the Constitution and can be amended without damaging its basic structure. Being secular, India is not a "religious" state — so Option 1 is wrong.
